impact: Facilitates effective onboarding of new student contributors and improves project accessibility.
evidence: The authors noted that the most effective projects involved in the program tagged specific beginner-friendly issues in their issue tracker.
CATEGORY: New Contributor Onboarding and Involvement | Community Collaboration and Engagement

article_title: **Lessons Learned Managing Distributed Software Engineering Courses**
actionable: Pair female participants together on projects to increase female representation.
impact: Increases female participation and support.
evidence: SC ensures that female participants are paired up on their projects.
CATEGORY: New Contributor Onboarding and Involvement | Community Collaboration and Engagement

article_title: **Lessons Learned Managing Distributed Software Engineering Courses**
actionable: Ensure each team includes students from diverse schools and geographic regions.
impact: Fosters diverse perspectives and collaboration.
evidence: SC ensures diversity of schools and geographic regions on each team.
CATEGORY: Community Collaboration and Engagement | Project Management and Governance

article_title: **Lessons Learned Managing Distributed Software Engineering Courses**
actionable: Hold a mentors‑only meeting before the sprint to review assessment processes and share mentoring strategies.
impact: Improves mentoring quality.
evidence: SC holds a mentors‑only meeting to provide mentors an overview of the assessment process and coaching opportunities.
CATEGORY: New Contributor Onboarding and Involvement | Project Management and Governance

article_title: **Lessons Learned Managing Distributed Software Engineering Courses**
actionable: Ensure each project maintains an active issue tracker, uses version control, and performs code reviews.
impact: Supports project health and student learning.
evidence: Projects must maintain active issue trackers, use version control, and perform code reviews.
CATEGORY: Code Standards and Maintainability | Project Management and Governance

article_title: **Lessons Learned Managing Distributed Software Engineering Courses**
actionable: Require each project to have an active development community and an active user community.
impact: Provides learning opportunities and motivates students.
evidence: Each project must have an active development community and an active user community.
CATEGORY: Community Collaboration and Engagement | Project Management and Governance

article_title: **Lessons Learned Managing Distributed Software Engineering Courses**
actionable: Set individual goals tailored to each student’s skills.
impact: Focuses on progress and personalized learning.
evidence: It is important that these goals are tailored for the individual skills of the student; being able to set individual goals for students with different knowledge and skills.
CATEGORY: New Contributor Onboarding and Involvement | Project Management and Governance

article_title: **Lessons Learned Managing Distributed Software Engineering Courses**
actionable: Require students to finalize their project contributions by the last day of class.
impact: Ensures completion before exams and prevents time buying.
evidence: Students are required to finalize their project contributions by their last day of class.

article_title: **Lessons Learned Managing Distributed Software Engineering Courses**
actionable: Require students to maintain a steady pace each week.
impact: Ensures consistent progress.
evidence: Students must maintain a steady pace each week.

article_title: **Lessons Learned Managing Distributed Software Engineering Courses**
actionable: Encourage faculty to connect regularly (bi‑weekly or weekly) with their students.
impact: Provides support and oversight.
evidence: Faculty are strongly encouraged to connect regularly (bi‑weekly or weekly) with their students.

article_title: **Lessons Learned Managing Distributed Software Engineering Courses**
actionable: Allocate at least 80% of the final grade to the work performed on UCOSP projects.
impact: Emphasizes project contribution.
evidence: The SC suggests that at least 80% of the final grade be attributed to the work performed on their projects.

actionable: Separate bot interactions into a dedicated tab or space in the pull request interface, distinct from human conversations.
impact: Prevents bots from interrupting human communication flow and allows developers to easily collapse or filter dead-ended bot messages.
evidence: 11 participants proposed separating bot comments; prototype testing showed 93% predicted future use and 87% preferred the designed interface over the traditional one.
CATEGORY: Community Collaboration and Engagement | Project Management and Governance

actionable: Summarize bot comments concisely in a single message.
impact: Mitigates information overload by providing an overview of pull request status.
evidence: 11 participants mentioned summarization as a key strategy (Table 2).
CATEGORY: Community Collaboration and Engagement | Documentation Practices

actionable: Prioritize bot comments based on task relevance or issue criticality.
impact: Helps developers focus on important information first.
evidence: Participants emphasized prioritization for tasks (IM3) and issues (IM4).

actionable: Explain project rules and requirements through the meta-bot.
impact: Guides newcomers and reduces confusion.
evidence: 8 participants mentioned explaining rules (NA1).
CATEGORY: New Contributor Onboarding and Involvement | Documentation Practices | Project Management and Governance

actionable: Schedule bot notifications to avoid interrupting developers during critical work periods.
impact: Reduces interruptions and improves workflow continuity.
evidence: 7 participants requested scheduling (NM2).
CATEGORY: Project Management and Governance | CI/CD and DevOps Automation

actionable: Implement a meta-bot as a mediator between existing bots and human developers on pull requests.
impact: Reduce noise and information overload caused by bots' interactions on pull requests, making it easier for developers to communicate and manage their workflow.
evidence: The fictional story and scenarios presented in the Design Fiction sessions indicated that a meta-bot could help mitigate the negative effects of bot notifications and messages on pull requests. Participants also provided feedback on the prototype, further supporting this recommendation.
CATEGORY: Community Collaboration and Engagement | CI/CD and DevOps Automation

actionable: Aggregate all bot comments into one consolidated comment.
impact: Reduces clutter and improves clarity of bot feedback.
evidence: 9 participants requested aggregation (IM2).

actionable: Keep only the most recent information from each bot, updating a single comment as new bot output arrives.
impact: Prevents outdated or duplicate information from cluttering the pull request.
evidence: 7 participants requested keeping the most recent info (IM5).

actionable: Categorize bot comments by type (e.g., testing, security, linting).
impact: Enables quick identification of comment type and relevance.
evidence: 5 participants requested categorization (IM6).
CATEGORY: Code Standards and Maintainability | Automated Testing and Quality Assurance | Security Best Practices and Legal Compliance

actionable: Provide a welcoming message for newcomers from the meta-bot.
impact: Enhances newcomer experience and project inclusivity.
evidence: 8 participants supported this strategy (NA2).
CATEGORY: New Contributor Onboarding and Involvement | Community Collaboration and Engagement

actionable: Notify developers through preferred channels (e.g., email, specific platforms).
impact: Reduces disruption by respecting user preferences.
evidence: 8 participants agreed on this approach (NM1).
CATEGORY: Community Collaboration and Engagement | Project Management and Governance

actionable: Detect and suppress repetitive or duplicate bot messages to prevent spam and information inflation on pull requests.
impact: Eliminates redundant notifications and reduces the cognitive load caused by multiple bots posting identical or highly similar comments.
evidence: 8 participants proposed preventing repetitive activities; the prototype's timeline reference feature was suggested to merge sequential bot comments into a single notification.
CATEGORY: Community Collaboration and Engagement | Project Management and Governance | CI/CD and DevOps Automation

actionable: Use summarization, aggregation, prioritization, categorization, and interaction with users through natural language in the meta-bot's communication.
impact: Improve the clarity and relevance of bot communications, reducing noise and information overload for developers.
evidence: These strategies were frequently mentioned by participants during Design Fiction sessions as ways to make bot communications more effective and less intrusive. The prototype also implemented these features, receiving positive feedback from participants.
CATEGORY: Community Collaboration and Engagement | Project Management and Governance

actionable: Implement a configuration dashboard allowing developers to customize notification channels, frequencies, and bot interaction preferences.
impact: Gives maintainers control over bot actions, reducing unwanted interruptions and accommodating diverse project needs.
evidence: 4 participants suggested a configuration dashboard; the study notes that OSS developers want to customize aspects like notification frequency and timing.

actionable: Implement internationalization support in the meta-bot's communication to promote diversity and inclusion.
impact: Enable developers from different linguistic backgrounds to better understand and interact with the meta-bot, fostering a more inclusive development environment.
evidence: Participants mentioned the importance of supporting multiple languages during Design Fiction sessions. While not explicitly stated in the prototype feedback, internationalization is a general best practice for improving accessibility and inclusivity.

actionable: Provide interactive, step‑by‑step information to newcomers about bot feedback.
impact: Guides newcomers through required actions, reducing errors.
evidence: 5 participants requested interactive info (NA3).
CATEGORY: New Contributor Onboarding and Involvement | Documentation Practices

actionable: Notify developers only during their idle times to avoid disrupting active work.
impact: Minimizes interruptions and respects developer focus.
evidence: 7 participants requested idle‑time notifications (NM3).
CATEGORY: Project Management and Governance | CI/CD and DevOps Automation

actionable: Delay maintainer notifications until all required conditions are satisfied.
impact: Prevents unnecessary notifications and reduces noise for maintainers.
evidence: 2 participants requested delayed maintainer notifications (NM5).
CATEGORY: Project Management and Governance | CI/CD and DevOps Automation

actionable: Report bugs in bot behavior to the bot maintainers automatically.
impact: Improves bot quality and reliability.
evidence: 2 participants requested bug reporting (SM3).
CATEGORY: Automated Testing and Quality Assurance | CI/CD and DevOps Automation

actionable: Include a link to the project's contributing guidelines in the meta‑bot message.
impact: Helps newcomers understand project rules and expectations.
evidence: 5 participants requested guideline links (PS9).
CATEGORY: New Contributor Onboarding and Involvement | Documentation Practices

actionable: Allow collapsing of bot outputs to reduce visual clutter.
impact: Reduces noise and improves readability of the pull request.
evidence: 5 participants requested collapsing (PS10).

actionable: Quote bot comments within the main conversation thread to maintain context.
impact: Preserves context and reduces confusion.
evidence: 5 participants requested quoting (PS12).

actionable: Move the bot summary to the main conversation thread for better visibility.
impact: Ensures developers see bot feedback without navigating tabs.
evidence: 4 participants requested moving the summary (PS13).

actionable: Offer an opt‑out option for interactive comments so users can choose a static view.
impact: Respects user preference and reduces cognitive load.
evidence: 3 participants requested opt‑out (PS14).

actionable: Rename the bots tab to a clearer name such as "Bot History" or "Bot Reports".
impact: Improves clarity of the interface for users.
evidence: 2 participants requested renaming (PS15).

actionable: Provide filtering options for bot interactions so users can focus on relevant bots.
impact: Improves relevance of notifications and reduces overload.
evidence: 1 participant requested filtering (PS11).
